# std.list

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Paged lists and builders.

## Types

### `ElementRef`

```badger
struct ElementRef<T> { page: list.Page, slot: Int }
```

A managed stable reference to one list element. It retains the element's
page, so the builder may keep appending (initialized slots never change)
and the reference stays valid after the list is finished or dropped.

#### `ElementRef.get`

```badger
fn get(self: &Self) -> T
```

### `filter_then_map`

```badger
fn filter_then_map<T, U>(list: List<T>, keep: fn(T) -> Bool, f: fn(T) -> U) -> List<U>
```

One pass for `filter(..).map(..)`: the compiler uses it when the filter
callback is side-effect free and cannot fail, so the eager and fused
callback orders are indistinguishable. `list` is walked once and no
intermediate list is built.

### `sort_by`

```badger
fn sort_by<T, K>(list: List<T>, key: fn(T) -> K) -> List<T> where K: PartialOrd
```

Sorted by `key`, stably (equal keys keep their order). O(n log n);
each key is computed once.

### `sort_with`

```badger
fn sort_with<T>(list: List<T>, compare: fn(T, T) -> Int) -> List<T>
```

Sorted by `compare` (negative: the first argument goes first; 0:
equal), stably. A bottom-up merge sort: O(n log n) comparisons.

Each pass merges into one contiguous buffer (`push` per element) and
freezes it into an array for the next pass, instead of rebuilding a paged
list every pass. Reads are direct array indexing.
